title: Cleopatra is closer to the Moon landing than to the pyramids

hook.onscreen: Was Cleopatra closer to the pyramids or the Moon landing?
hook.voiceover: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.

stories.voiceover: The Great Pyramid of Giza went up around twenty-six hundred B.C. Cleopatra died in thirty B.C.
That's a gap of about two and a half thousand years.
Now jump forward from her death to the Moon landing, in nineteen sixty-nine. Only about two thousand years.
So to Cleopatra, the pyramid was more ancient than she is to you today.

math.year_convention: BC years converted to astronomical numbering (1 BC = year 0) so gaps are exact: astro(y) = y + 1 for BC years given as negative numbers
math.pyramid_to_cleopatra: Great Pyramid c. 2600 BC (astro -2599) -> Cleopatra's death 30 BC (astro -29): -29 - (-2599) = 2570 years (said: about two and a half thousand)
math.pyramid_range_check: With published estimates of completion from 2700 BC to 2484 BC the gap is 2670 to 2454 years; always > 1998 and > 2055, so the claim holds for every estimate
math.cleopatra_to_moon: 30 BC (astro -29) -> 20 July 1969: 1969 - (-29) = 1998 years (said: about two thousand)
math.cleopatra_to_today: 30 BC -> 2026: 2026 - (-29) = 2055 years, which is less than 2570 (and less than the 2454 minimum), so the pyramid was older to her than she is to us
math.difference: 2570 - 1998 = 572 years closer to the Moon landing; ratio 2570 / 1998 = 1.29
math.pyramid_sources: Wikipedia: built c. 2600 BC over ~26 years; National Geographic: Khufu began it circa 2550 BC (~4,500 years ago). Gap to 30 BC: 2570 (2600 BC) or 2520 (2550 BC) -> 'about two and a half thousand years'
math.cleopatra_death: 30 BC (Wikipedia: 10 or 12 August 30 BC; History.com: August 12, 30 B.C.)
